what: File Locker encrypts any files with a password into one .gtnlock file, and unlocks it back to the exact original files, with their original names. Photos, PDFs, videos, documents and whole sets of files all work.

Everything happens on your device with the browser's built-in Web Crypto: AES-256-GCM encryption and a key made from your password with PBKDF2-SHA256 and 600,000 rounds. Big files are handled in 4 MB pieces, each with its own tamper check, so even files of a gigabyte or more work without filling the memory.
Your files are never uploaded. Nobody can recover a lost password, so keep it safe.
uses: Protect files on a USB stick
Lock tax papers or ID scans before copying them to a stick that might get lost.
Send private files by email or cloud
Attach the .gtnlock file and tell the person the password on a call.
Store locked copies in a cloud drive so the provider cannot read them.
Keep a set of files together
Lock many files into one .gtnlock file; unlocking gives back every file with its name.
Files of hundreds of megabytes are locked in seconds on a computer.
tutorial: Click the box or drop files on it. Add as many as you like; the list shows each file and the total size. Use ✕ to remove one.
Type a password twice. The bar shows how strong it is. Four or more random words are strong and easy to remember.
Press "Lock files". The progress bar shows how far it is. Press Stop to cancel.
Press Download. One file is named like the original with .gtnlock added; several files become "first-file-and-2-more.gtnlock".
Before deleting any originals, choose "Unlock a .gtnlock file", pick the locked file, type the password and check the files come back.
Come back to this page, choose Unlock, pick the .gtnlock file, type the password and press Unlock. Download each file, or press Download all.
features: With a PBKDF2-SHA256 key (600,000 rounds), a random 16-byte salt and a random 12-byte IV for every file you make.
Data is locked in 4 MB pieces, each with its own tag, so 1 GB files work in a browser that allows them.
A changed, swapped, cut-off or incomplete piece is detected, and nothing is unlocked from a damaged file.
The original file names, including non-English names, are stored inside the encrypted part.
Lock a whole set of files into a single .gtnlock file.
See the percentage, size done and time left, and cancel any time.
Every file starts with GTNLOCK and a version number so it can be opened by later versions of the tool.

example.title: Worked example: sending scanned documents to an accountant
example.text: You have three PDFs: passport.pdf, payslip-may.pdf and bank-statement.pdf, 6 MB in total. You add them, choose the password "window cactus seven harbour" and press Lock files. A moment later you download passport-and-2-more.gtnlock and attach it to an email. You phone your accountant and tell them the password. They open this page, choose Unlock, pick the file, type the password and get all three PDFs back with the same names.

tips: Write the password down somewhere safe. Without it the files are gone for good.
Unlock a test copy before you delete the original files.
Send the password a different way from the file: say it on a call or in person.
On phones, very large files (over 1 GB) may run out of memory or space; use a computer for those.
Renaming the .gtnlock file is fine; the original names are stored inside it.
problems: Check the password, including capital letters and spaces. If it is right, the file was changed or did not finish downloading; try another copy.
"The password is right, but the file is damaged or incomplete"
Part of the file was changed or lost after locking, for example an interrupted download. Nothing is unlocked. Get a complete copy.
"Not a file locked with File Locker"
Choose the .gtnlock file made on this page, not the original file.
It stops or the page reloads with very large files
The device ran out of memory or storage. Close other tabs, free some space, lock fewer files at a time, or use a computer.
